statement: Kim has three number cards: 3, 0 and 7. She uses two of the cards to make a two-digit number. What is the smallest number she can make?

choices.misconception: I used the card 3 twice, but there is only one 3 card.
I thought the 0 card cannot be used, so I used 3 and 7.
I made the biggest number instead of the smallest.
I used all three cards, but she uses only two.

hints: Can a two-digit number start with 0?
Make the tens digit as small as you can, then the ones digit. Remember that a number written with 0 in front is really a one-digit number.
The tens digit cannot be 0, so the smallest tens digit is 3. Now pick the smallest card left for the ones.

solutions.reliable: The tens digit matters most, so make it small. It cannot be 0, because 07 is just 7, a one-digit number. So the tens digit is 3, and the smallest card left is 0, giving 30. The idea to keep: the left digit counts most, and 0 cannot lead.

whyOnTest: Zero can sit in the ones place but never lead a two-digit number, a place-value point several choices are built around.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
